ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure shows a thin square slab/sheet drawn in perspective. The long in-plane dimension is labeled L with horizontal arrows, and the small thickness is labeled t with vertical arrows. The shaded/hatched regions are two opposite narrow edge faces of the sheet. Reasoning: The resistance is between these two opposite shaded faces, so current travels across the sheet from one shaded face to the other over a length L. The cross-sectional area perpendicular to this current is the area of a shaded narrow face, which is L × t. Using R = ρℓ/A gives R = ρL/(Lt) = ρ/t. Therefore the factor L cancels.

raw_record.question_text: Consider a thin square sheet of side L and thickness t, made of a material of resistivity ρ. How does the resistance between the two opposite shaded faces shown in the figure depend on L?

method.method_draft: First describe the figure: it shows a thin square sheet drawn as a slab, with the horizontal dimension labeled L and the vertical small thickness labeled t; the shaded regions are two opposite narrow side faces of the slab. From the text, take the material resistivity as ρ and the sheet side length as L. Treat current as flowing from one shaded face to the opposite shaded face across a distance L. The conducting cross-sectional area perpendicular to this current is the area of one shaded face, L × t. Apply R = ρ\ell/A, giving R = ρ L/(L t) = ρ/t, so the dependence on L cancels and the resistance is independent of L.
